chapter_title: Concerning Wisdom; it is far superior when on the Tongue than in the Heart of the Person.
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by a non-institutional teaching unit (child-in-womb and fire-in-wood analogies) explaining why wisdom increases when expressed. The main late material is the Kephalaia dialogue apparatus (disciple petitions, apostle-attribution formulas, and the formulaic closing). No NT citation overlay and no ecclesial/pastoral graft is present; the core here is homiletic-correspondential rather than systematic cosmological mapping.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Strong Q&A frame: “Once again… disciple… before the apostle… I entreat you, my master.” Even though it paraphrases the topic, the paragraph functions as editorial setup rather than impersonal teaching exposition.
Continues the editorial question apparatus (disciple speech + repeated entreaty). This reads as an eliciting prompt and self-report rather than the teaching layer’s own expository voice.

paragraphs.core_text: Well [do] you ask! And great is this lesson for which you have sought, [that is] whence comes my great joy, on account of this wis-dom that I utter? [ ... ] it is superior in my mouth when I proclaim it than when it is set in m[y heart]. You yourself rejoice in it; and the other one who hears it from you, he shall rejoice in it, and be enlightened [by] it and receive thereby permanent strength.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution: “Then the apostle speaks to that disciple:” (Kephalaia compilation frame using the title “apostle”).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The attribution formula is late frame, but the remaining content is a compact teaching maxim about the effect of proclamation (joy/enlightenment/strength) without institutional or NT anchoring.

paragraphs.core_text: For like this matter, just so a small b[o]y who is conceived in the belly of his mother. He [ ... he] turns in his mother's womb, filling her womb. The mother knows and understands that this child she conceives is alive within her. She rejoices over him until [the tim]e when she gives birth. And he comes from her alive with his [limbs whole] and perfect in beauty, without defect, [in] the living open air that is more sp[ac]ious than the first air he was in. He fills his eyes with the light and speaks with his living voice in the way of they who are born.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal analogical exposition (no dialogue formula, no institutional targets). The teaching proceeds by correspondence (womb→hidden life; birth→manifestation; air/light/voice→manifest life).

paragraphs.core_text: Now, the time when this woman conceives the child in her belly, her joy at conceiving him in her womb is not so [ve]ry great as when she gives birth and sees him; and is full of his [be]auty and stature in the space of a single moment. The love and joy over him shall be a hundred [t]imes greater than it was, now that she has given birth and seen him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same simile as structured teaching (concealment vs manifestation), without frame/pastoral directives.

paragraphs.core_text: For the first time when she conceived him in her belly, his beauty and the sight of his eyes was hidden from his m[o/th]er; but when she gave birth to him she saw his beauty. His s[t]ature and his loveliness came before the e[ye]s of his f[athe]r [a]nd his mother and all his relatives. They shall rejoic[e] over him more and more when they look upon him face to face and see his beauty and delightfulness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still purely analogical-causal explanation (hidden/seen; face to face) with no editorial anchoring to community practice.

paragraphs.core_text: Just as in this simile, the wisdom that is present [in] the heart of the person is like the living child who is co[nceived] in the belly of his mother. And when he is taught and seals it in his heart, it becomes like the child who shall be born, and they see his beauty.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Explicit correspondence mapping (wisdom-in-heart ↔ conceived child; proclamation/manifestation implied by birth). This stays within the teaching’s internal symbolic system (no cosmos→institution pointing).

paragraphs.core_text: So, in this way, the wisdom that the person proclaims, speak[ng] it from his heart, shall be advanced more and mor[e]. Its en-hancement and glory shall double from the time when the bea-uty and splendour of the saying will be displayed before the eyes [of t]hey who hear it, and it shall also advance for you [ ... ... ] your hearing, and you are astonished at what you proclai[m].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Process-teaching voice (advance/double/displayed), focused on how utterance amplifies wisdom through hearing—no later institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, the wisdom is like this, while it is hidden in the heart of the person. [Bef]ore he has uttered it, it is just like [the blaze] of fire that is hidden in wood. An[d] that wood is [set aflame] by the blaze of the fire, but the garment of fir[e that exists in] the wood is not apparent. Indeed, you can see [ ... ] wood and they put them in a single house. It is impossible to [put li]ght to that house as long as the light within [ ... ] until the time when they are added to the fire, and the light [comes f]orth from them. It is possible for that entire house [to be] lit by the light of a single piece of wood.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second sustained analogy (fire-in-wood) used as correspondential mechanics (hidden potency vs manifest light) without editorial polemic or church discipline.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also the case with the wisdom that is in the heart of the person. [It] is like the fire that is hidden in the wood, as its light is not [d]isplayed. For its part, the wisdom is like this: its li[ght] is hidden and its glory is hidden in the heart; but when the person will proclaim it, its glory shall be displayed before the eyes and the ears of a multitude.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Direct interpretive mapping of the simile (hidden light/glory → displayed to eyes/ears). Still not cosmos→institution, and no citation formulas.
Returns to the Kephalaia dialogue apparatus (“Once again… disciple… speaks to the apostle”) introducing a second question; functions as editorial staging.
Attribution and promise-to-explain (“the apostle speaks… I will persuade you…”) with no teaching substance; typical dialogue frame linkage.

paragraphs.core_text: For in this respect the wisdom is like this child about whom I have told you, the one who [was] born from the woman. Now, when he will be born, his father and mother and family circle shall rejoice over him. However, you find others grieving by reason of him, [s]ince they are strangers to him. These are not reckoned among his family. [They do n]ot rejoice over him, because he is not of their race.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extends the analogy internally (kin vs strangers) to explain differential reception; no ecclesial categories (elect/auditors) are introduced.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also [the case] with the wisdom. When it is proclaimed by the mouth of the teacher, these who are [a]kin to it shall receive it to them and rejoice in it; but [those] who are strangers to it neither rejoice in it [ ... ] nor receive it to them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Interpretive mapping of the kin/stranger simile to wisdom-hearers. “teacher” is generic here (not an office list), and the mapping stays within the teaching logic.

paragraphs.core_text: Just like the light of [the fire, which I] proclaim[ed] to you, that shall come from the wood [and be apparent o]utside before the eyes of every one. So, [wh]oever looks shall see the light that has [come fro]m the wood; but whoever is blind does not see the [fir]e.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Analogy extension (seeing vs blindness) remains general and non-institutional, preparing the doctrinal criterion in the next paragraph.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also the case with the wisdom, when it will be pro-claimed. The person, in whom is the [Mi]nd, of him is the wisdom. Whenever he may hear it, he shall receive it in to him; but the one who has no Mind in him is a stranger to it. He neither receives it in to him, nor shall he listen to [it].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Introduces an internal, system-consistent criterion (presence/absence of Mind as an ontic capacity) rather than institutional identity; this reads as teaching substance rather than later pastoral regulation.
Formulaic closing reaction (“rejoiced… made obeisance… sat down”), matching the chapter-level ‘formulaic closing’ flag; classic hagiographic wrap-up.
